newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia grain receivals resume after rains.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia grain receivals resume after rains.

text.p: Widespread rain in New South Wales halted grain receivals in many harvesting areas late last week and over the weekend before recommencing on Monday, New South Wales grain handler GrainCorp said on Tuesday.

Despite the rain, GrainCorp said it received close to 850,000 tonnes of grain last week, bringing total receivals up to six million tonnes. Graincorp estimates that between 900,000 and 1.1 million tonnes of grain remains to be received.

The rains so far have not prompted calls for "falling number" testing equipment at silos, although follow-up rains could cause damage in some eastern regions of the state, GrainCorp said. In northern sectors, the rain provided welcome moisture for summer crops, it said.
GrainCorp said the heavy rains -- close to four inches fell on the Liverpool Plains -- provided an opportunity to overflow grain, creating additional storage space at many silos.
Also, over the weekend, GrainCorp transported over 80,000 tonnes of grain to sub-terminals and ports, it said.
Many growers took advantage of the break in harvesting to make deliveries from on-farm storages, it said.
GrainCorp spokesman Bill O'Connor told Reuters he expects the current grains harvest to conclude by late December.
